places.name: Mundeshwari Devi Temple
places.description: One of the oldest functional Hindu temples in India, dating back to 108 AD. Perched atop Mundeshwari Hill, it is dedicated to Goddess Mundeshwari and Lord Shiva. The octagonal structure is a marvel of ancient architecture that has withstood centuries of history.
details: Located on Mundeshwari Hill, ~608m above sea level
Octagonal structure unique in Indian temple architecture

places.name: Karakat Waterfall
places.description: A breathtaking cascade hidden in the lush forests of the Kaimur range. The waterfall is especially spectacular during and after the monsoon season, drawing nature lovers and trekkers from across Bihar.
details: Surrounded by dense Sal and Teak forests
Short trek required from the road

places.name: Telhar Waterfall
places.description: A serene and lesser-known waterfall nestled in the rocky terrain of Kaimur. The crystal-clear water tumbles over ancient rocks, creating a peaceful retreat perfect for picnics and photography.

places.name: Maa Mundeshwari Eco Park
places.description: Take a relaxing break at Maa Mundeshwari Eco Park, a green space near the famous Mundeshwari temple. Its landscaped entrance, wildlife sculptures, and wooded hill surroundings make it a pleasant stop for families and visitors exploring the area.
places.highlight: A peaceful nature stop near the temple
details: Green, landscaped setting among the hills
A scenic spot for a relaxed walk and photos
Pair your visit with nearby Maa Mundeshwari Temple

places.name: Durgawati Reservoir
places.description: Built on the Durgawati River, this reservoir is surrounded by the Kaimur hills and dense forests. It is a haven for migratory birds and offers stunning sunset views, making it ideal for birdwatching and nature walks.
details: Home to migratory birds in winter
Stunning sunset views over the hills
